flags.title: Amazon edited the listing title; the stored wording and the live wording differ
flags.what: The Emeril Lagasse listing (B09B7SB46R) served 'Countertop Convection Cooker, 24 One-Touch Preset Options, Extra Large Interior, Six Cooking Accessories Included' on 2026-11-16. data/products.json and marketing/index.html still carry the 2026-11-13/14 wording ('French doors, 24 cooking functions, dual-speed fan and rotisserie for easy family meals'). The listing's own URL slug still contains 'dual-speed-rotisserie', so the live title and the live slug disagree with each other.
flags.why_it_matters: Any page that promises rotisserie or a dual-speed fan for this machine is quoting wording that is not in the title today. This site publishes neither.
flags.action: Decide whether to refresh the stored titles from a same-day capture (they will drift again), or keep dating every quotation, as the guides do. Nothing was overwritten.

flags.title: The release gate cannot fail on disclosure, disclaimer, single-h1 or row-provenance checks
flags.what: tools/verify_site.py builds its 'owned pages' set from data/z3/build-manifest.json's 'files' values, but those values are 12-character content digests (e.g. agent-terms: 94cb0fee17a9), not paths. No page is ever matched, so V1/V2/V3/V4 findings are demoted to advisory for the whole repository. Reproduced on 2026-11-16 with a synthetic page missing the disclosure sentence and carrying an unsourced table row: those checks reported only as advisory and the exit code came from an unrelated 'sitemap.xml missing' error.
flags.why_it_matters: 'VERIFY PASS' on this repository has been read as evidence that disclosure and row-provenance rules hold. It is not. The rules do hold today — this session checked them independently — but the gate would not have caught it if they did not.
flags.action: Recommended: have tools/build_site.py record generated_paths in the manifest, make verify_site.py read that, and land it as its own PR because the corrected gate will turn inherited pages' advisory items into hard failures. Compensating control shipped now: tools/cba81fa5_lint.py fails the build on the same checks over site/**.

flags.title: Two reader sites, two brands, overlapping topics
flags.what: /read/ ('The Crisp Report', 11 pages, images, JSON-LD, session d18303ca) and /site/ ('Air Fryer Field Notes', 18 pages including the four guides, the open-questions register and the house style, sessions 59d84c55 and cba81fa5) both answer the same shopper questions from the same three listings, published on the same day. read/capacity.html and site/guides/capacity-maths.html are the clearest overlap, as are the cleaning, features and best-seller pages.
flags.why_it_matters: A reader who finds both sees the same argument twice from two names, and search engines see two near-duplicate sets. The board has flagged duplicate registers for the same reason; this is the reader-facing version of it.
flags.action: Owner decision (question Q-12 in site/answers.html): adopt one brand as canonical and keep the other as an internal verification set, or merge the two guide sets into one nav. This session took the middle path: the root front door points at /read/ for reading, /site/ keeps the evidence desk and the decision board, and site/guides/index.html labels itself a second-source check. Nothing was deleted.

flags.title: 22 lint findings inherited from other sessions' reader pages
flags.what: Blank-state rows on site/products.html (Price, Star rating, Review count, Availability, Commission for this product, Trend rank / demand, Conversion rate) carry no source cell; Amazon's bounty amounts are rendered on a product-facing page; and two pages quote the constructions they forbid in a form the mechanical rule matched before the use/mention rule was added.
flags.why_it_matters: The rows are honest content in the wrong place: a row that explains what is not published still needs the rule it is standing on, or the next reader cannot tell a deliberate blank from a missing value.
flags.action: Owners of those pages: move the 'cannot publish' rows into a note block or add the Participation Requirements link, and put quoted-ban examples in <span class="example">. The findings are listed in tools/cba81fa5_lint-baseline.json and reported on every run as advisory.
